cumulativeExperimentNote: If CG-13 R1 produces DIVERGES=0, the frozen contract will have been tested against electric (CG-10), gas (CG-11), induction (CG-12), and dual-fuel (CG-13) without canonical mutation — a clean architectural experiment.

frozenContractUnderTest.note: electric_range.json is immutable contract truth for CG-13. Dual-fuel evidence may fit, falsify, or document boundary — it may not teach the frozen contract merely by being different.

centerpieceQuestion.question: Can the frozen electric_range rev1 functional ontology represent a dual-fuel range — gas surface heating with an electric oven — without canonical divergence?
centerpieceQuestion.framing: CG-13 is potentially the strongest fit test yet — one appliance combines two fundamentally different surface/oven energy architectures. The question is functional representation, not whether unseen hardware exists.
allowedOutcomes: dual_fuel_fits — frozen contract absorbs dual-fuel functional architecture with platform overlay vocabulary only
partial_fit — documented boundary extensions without mutating frozen electric rev1
dual_fuel_diverges — dual-fuel exposes functional architecture the frozen contract cannot absorb; document boundary, do not mutate electric
centerpieceQuestion.disallowedShortcut: Promoting gas surface hardware to canonical because the appliance is dual-fuel, creating dual_fuel_range.json, or treating combined fuel types as requiring a new ontology file

criticalDualFuelProbe.question: Does combining gas surface heating and electric oven heating create a functional dependency that the frozen contract cannot represent?
criticalDualFuelProbe.notTheQuestion: Are there components we haven't seen before? There absolutely will be — that is expected platform vocabulary.
